articles.summary: Ela foi eleita para os Halls da Fama do Country e do Rock & Roll e ganhou 10 prêmios no Grammy. Informação foi revelada pelo sobrinho da cantora nas redes sociais.
articles.body:
Lenda da música country, a cantora e atriz Dolly Parton morreu nesta terça (25), aos 80 anos. A informação foi confirmada pela família em um vídeo nas redes sociais.

"Esse anúncio em vídeo é algo que Dolly me pediu há anos, antes que eu tivesse absorvido totalmente como uma realidade no futuro", disse Bryan Seaver, sobrinho e chefe da segurança da cantora.

"A tristeza fica conosco, não com a Dolly. Dolly viveu na luz e está nos braços de Jesus, com certeza, ao lado de Carl [Thomas Dean, seu marido, que morreu em 2025], seus pais e incontáveis outros que a assistiram e que queriam encontrá-la nos céus."

Em último vídeo nas redes sociais, Dolly Parton convidou para exposição sobre sua vida; veja

Relembre história de 'Jolene', clássico da cantora que ganhou versão de Beyoncé

"Dolly também abriu as portas para gerações de cantores, compositores, músicos e sonhadores de todos os campos da vida e de todos os continentes. Com seu exemplo, nós acreditamos que tudo era possível. Ela nunca viu uma porta que não pudesse abrir, e as portas que ela abriu fizeram e mudaram a história."

Dolly enfrentava problemas de saúde desde a morte do marido, Carl Dean, que morreu em março de 2025. Ela cancelou uma residência de shows em maio deste ano. Em entrevista à revista "People", publicada no dia 21, ela disse que "não prestou atenção [aos próprios problemas]" enquanto cuidava do marido.

"Mas ainda estou trabalhando e há muitas coisas que eu ainda quero conquistar", acrescentou.

Conhecida pela voz marcante, pelas perucas loiras e por seus figurinos extravagantes, Dolly construiu um império no entretenimento a partir de suas origens humildes no estado americano do Tennessee.

Com mais de 3 mil músicas em seu catálogo, a artista se consolidou como um ícone da cultura pop e expandiu sua atuação para além da música country, transitando pelo pop, bluegrass e pela era disco.

Sua trajetória na música e no cinema se tornou parte do cânone da cultura americana. Ao longo de sua carreira, Dolly compôs sucessos atemporais que se tornaram clássicos, regravados por artistas do calibre de Beyoncé e Tina Turner. São dela músicas como "Jolene", "9 to 5" e "Coat of Many Colors".

Também foi Dolly quem escreveu e lançou a balada romântica "I Will Always Love You", posteriormente gravada por Whitney Houston para o filme "O Guarda-Costas".

Dolly Parton durante evento em Nova York, em outubro de 2022 — Foto: AP Photo/Andres Kudacki, Arquivo

Nascida em 1946 em Sevier County, em uma cabana de apenas um cômodo às margens do rio Little Pigeon, Dolly era a quarta de 12 filhos de um agricultor sem terras. A família não tinha acesso a água encanada ou eletricidade, e o médico que atendeu seu parto foi pago com um saco de farinha de milho.

Foi no ambiente familiar, marcado por hinos e canções folclóricas ensinadas pela mãe, que ela aprendeu a tocar instrumentos como violão e banjo, fazendo suas primeiras apresentações no rádio ainda na infância e lançando seu primeiro compacto em 1959.

O primeiro grande avanço em sua carreira ocorreu em 1967, ao ser contratada para o programa de televisão do cantor Porter Wagoner. A parceria na TV rendeu diversos hits em dueto, mas a crescente popularidade solo de Dolly acabou superando a do parceiro.

Ao decidir deixar o programa para focar na carreira solo em 1974, ela compôs "I Will Always Love You" como uma homenagem de despedida. A faixa alcançou o topo da parada country duas vezes antes de se tornar um fenômeno pop na voz de Whitney Houston, em 1992.

Ao longo de mais de seis décadas de trajetória, a artista escreveu cerca de 3 mil músicas. Suas composições abordavam temas cotidianos com olhar empático e socialmente crítico, tratando da infância pobre em "Coat of Many Colors", da gravidez na adolescência em "Down From Dover" e do machismo no mercado de trabalho em "9 to 5", canção-tema do filme homônimo lançado em 1980 no qual ela também atuou ao lado de Jane Fonda e Lily Tomlin.

Lily Tomlin, Dolly Parton e Jane Fonda em '9 to 5' — Foto: Reprodução

Entre seus maiores sucessos nas paradas estão a colaboração com Kenny Rogers em "Islands in the Stream" (1983) e o aclamado projeto "Trio", gravado ao lado de Emmylou Harris e Linda Ronstadt. A artista também construiu um império empresarial no Tennessee com o parque temático Dollywood e investiu na indústria cinematográfica e na televisão.

Com 55 indicações ao Grammy e 10 vitórias, Parton também foi a terceira mulher mais indicada na história do Grammy, atrás apenas de Beyoncé e Taylor Swift.

Dolly não tinha medo de inovar ou experimentar em seu trabalho, o que a garantiu essa carreira tão versátil e duradoura.

“Eu não tinha medo de mudar. Eu esperava o sucesso, mas estava preparada para o fracasso. Não me importava se as pessoas achassem que eu estava errada. No fundo, eu sabia que estava fazendo a coisa certa", disse à Associated Press em 1979.

Eleita para os Halls da Fama do Country e do Rock & Roll, Dolly Parton também se destacou pela atuação filantrópica. Por meio da fundação Imagination Library, criada em 1995, ela distribuiu mais de 200 milhões de livros para crianças.

Defensora ativa da diversidade e da inclusão, a cantora aliou seu trabalho social a posicionamentos públicos acolhedores, tornando-se uma figura de apelo universal na música norte-americana.

Nas últimas décadas, conquistou novas gerações ao trabalhar com artistas como Miley Cyrus, de quem era madrinha, Sabrina Carpenter e Beyoncé.

articles.title: Após cancelar turnê, Xamã lança álbum, 'Flerte', em que canta com Ludmilla, NP Vocal, L7nnon, Amabii e Nomad | G1
articles.body:
Capa do álbum 'Flerte', de Xamã — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Duas semanas após ter cancelado, às vésperas da estreia, uma turnê que previa mais de 30 shows em 25 cidades do Brasil, Xamã se prepara para apresentar o quinto álbum de estúdio do artista, intitulado “Flerte” e programado para ser lançado na quinta-feira, 27 de agosto.

“Foram onze meses construindo esse universo com recortes de poesias escritas no bloco de notas, músicas regravadas, pessoas e texturas que fizeram esse desejo ganhar forma”, relatou o cantor e compositor carioca ao revelar a capa e a contracapa – esta com a tracklist – do álbum “Flerte”.

Além dos já conhecidos feats com Ludmilla (em “Moça”) e L7nnon (em “Tá de parabéns”), faixas lançadas em julho e em março, respectivamente, o álbum “Flerte” traz as músicas “Bagunçou minha sexta”, “Like a Michael”, “Meu sonho é tu”, “Chá de”, “Você tirou meu ar” e “A nova sagitariana”, totalizando oito faixas.

Três delas – “A nova sagitariana”, “Chá de” e “Você tirou meu ar”– trazem a rapper paulistana Amabii (artista que transita entre o rap e o R&B) e o rapper NP Vocal. O carioca Nomad se junta a Amabii e a NP Vocal em “Chá de”.

A produção musical do álbum “Flerte” foi orquestrada por Ramon Calixto, $amuka e Marcio Arantes.

articles.title: Inside Jaaved Jaaferiâs 7,000-sq-ft sea-facing Bandra home with Mediterranean design, earthy interiors, textured walls, family memories and breathtaking Arabian Sea views

articles.body: For veteran actor and television personality Jaaved Jaaferi, home has always meant Bandra. The actor graciously recently opened the doors of his over 7,000-square-foot sea-facing apartment, walking Architectural Digest through a thoughtful space that reflects both his personal history and his family's evolving lifestyle needs. Designed by Kush Bhayani of KULx Studio, the spacious home leans into a warm, Mediterranean aesthetic while weaving in decades of memories from Jaaved's life in the suburb.Jaaved Jafferi's return to Bandra, rooted in nostalgiaJaaved's move back to Bandra wasn't just about the address but was deeply personal. "I've been a Bandra boy all my life; I was here for 40 years," Jaaved shares, recalling how he split his childhood and early years between his first two homes in the suburb before eventually moving to Lokhandwala with his children.The decision to return was also influenced by his elder children, Meezaan and Alaviaa. While Jaaved once found Bandra's dense construction overwhelming, this particular apartment changed his mind instantly. His brief to designer Kush Bhayani was simple: minimal sophistication, described in three words â "Warm, natural, eclectic."The new residence consequently became a way of reconnecting with familiar surroundings while creating a contemporary family home.What does Jaaved Jafferi's home look like?Overlooking the Arabian Sea, the apartment is designed around earthy, sunbaked tones that give it an instantly calming quality. The living room is anchored by a sage-toned two-sided sofa, while plush, earth-toned furnishings and pops of green create a soothing, lived-in atmosphere. The interiors draw heavily from Mediterranean influences, with earthy shades and natural materials running throughout the apartment. The expansive living room features plush, earth-toned furnishings, complemented by green accents that give the space a calm and soothing character.Textured micro-concrete walls run through the entire home, a detail the whole family agrees on. Patterned rugs, cured wood logs and translucent stone surfaces add to the eclectic, rustic-meets-modern feel, while a cosy reading nook with a built-in bookshelf houses artefacts from the family's travels and an extensive DVD collection.The dining table and family spaces at Jaaved Jafferi's homeOne addition the family was especially keen on was a proper dining table, something increasingly rare in homes shaped by social media and OTT habits. Meezaan explains the shift it's brought about at home, noting that everyone now gathers to eat together instead of retreating to their rooms with their meals. The dining area features a sleek onyx slab table supported by wooden logs, paired with upholstered chairs, and lit by bespoke sculptural fabric pendant lamps.A long terrace serves as another favourite spot, where two generations of the family come together to talk and unwind. Alaviaa's room, meanwhile, stands out with rust-maroon and colourful accents against the home's earthy base, including a statement chair and a sinuous mirror.A reading nook filled with family memoriesThe apartment also makes space for Jaaved's love of nostalgia. A cosy reading corner incorporates a built-in bookshelf filled with artefacts collected during the family's travels, along with an extensive DVD collection. Objects bearing personal significance have been integrated into the interiors. The family's shared history is similarly reflected in Meezaan's collection of CDs, featuring artists such as Don McLean and Fleetwood Mac. The collection was gifted to him by his father.The terrace overlooking the Arabian SeaThe home's terrace provides perhaps its most striking setting. Stretching along the apartment, it offers the family an open space to unwind, converse and spend time together while looking out towards the Arabian Sea. For Jaaved, the terrace and the home as a whole represent a connection between different stages of his life, his childhood in Bandra, his years as a performer and his present life surrounded by his children.More about Jaaved Jaaferi's workOn the professional front, Jaaved Jaaferi has had a busy run through 2025 and 2026. He featured in the psychological thriller 'Mayasabha â The Hall of Illusion', directed by Rahi Anil Barve, which released in theatres on January 30, 2026. He also appeared in 'De De Pyaar De 2' and 'Inn Galiyon Mein'. Most recently, Jaaved returned to the comedy franchise that made him a household name with 'Dhamaal 4', reuniting with Ajay Devgn, Riteish Deshmukh, Arshad Warsi and Sanjay Mishra, which released around Eid 2026. He also has projects including 'Love & War' and 'Hera Pheri 3' in various stages of production.Give your child the gift of confidence! Claim your exclusive TOI Masterclass spot today!

The festival, also known as Rakhi, falls on the full moon day, or Purnima Tithi, of the Hindu month of Shravana.If you're wondering when to tie the Rakhi, what the shubh muhurat is and what you need for the traditional puja, here's a simple guide.Raksha Bandhan 2026: Date and Purnima TithiAccording to Drik Panchang, Raksha Bandhan falls on August 28, 2026.The Purnima Tithi begins at 9:08 am on August 27 and ends at 9:48 am on August 28.There's a reason you may find slightly different Rakhi timings online. Hindu festival timings are worked out according to the local sunrise and other Panchang calculations, so the muhurat isn't necessarily identical in every city.Raksha Bandhan 2026: Shubh MuhuratFor New Delhi, the Rakhi-tying muhurat on August 28 is from 5:57 am to 9:48 am.That's a little over three and a half hours, giving families plenty of time to get together and perform the ceremony.The Bhadra period ends before sunrise in New Delhi on August 28, so it doesn't overlap with this Rakhi-tying window.If you're celebrating outside Delhi, though, check the Panchang for your own city before deciding on the timing.Raksha Bandhan 2026: Rakhi-Tying TimingsThe timing changes slightly depending on the city.In Mumbai, for instance, the Rakhi-tying muhurat is 6:22 am to 9:48 am on August 28, according to Drik Panchang.You might also see Choghadiya timings listed for the day. But those shouldn't automatically be taken as the Rakhi-tying muhurat. The two aren't necessarily the same.And if your family traditionally avoids Rahu Kaal for auspicious ceremonies, remember that this timing also depends on the city.Mumbai Raksha Bandhan 2026 TimingsRaksha Bandhan: Friday, August 28, 2026Rakhi-tying muhurat: 6:22 am to 9:48 amPurnima Tithi begins: August 27 at 9:08 amPurnima Tithi ends: August 28 at 9:48 amBhadra: Ends before sunrise on August 28These are Mumbai-specific timings. If you're celebrating somewhere else, use the Panchang for your city.Raksha Bandhan 2026: Puja VidhiThe actual Rakhi ceremony is pretty straightforward.After the morning bath and other daily rituals, the family can get the puja thali ready. Usually, it includes the Rakhi, roli or kumkum, akshat, a diya and some sweets.The brother sits down for the ceremony and the sister applies a tilak to his forehead, followed by akshat. She then performs the aarti and prays for his health, happiness and long life.Then comes the moment everyone is waiting for - she ties the Rakhi around his wrist and offers him sweets.The brother traditionally gives his sister a gift in return. And, depending on the family, there may be hugs, teasing, photographs and a lot of catching up afterwards.That's also why there isn't one rigid way to celebrate Raksha Bandhan. Customs can differ from family to family and region to region. articles.title: Food influencers v critics: Why credibility counts
articles.summary: People on the food scene look at the rise of influencers and the role of social media in the industry.
articles.body:
When stuck for ideas about where to eat on a Friday night or torn between takeaways, more and more people are turning to social media and their favourite content creators for inspiration.

Research by one Bristol food writer has raised questions about transparency, with some creators guaranteeing positive coverage in advance and offering not to make clear their review was in exchange for a free meal.

Those promises of good reviews were made before they had eaten a bite - or realised the restaurant they had been asked to promote did not exist.

So can diners trust influencers to give an honest opinion and what is their role in shaping where we eat? We asked people in the food scene to share their thoughts.

Strangers at festival help autistic man realise dream

Travellers' camp mess causes football club disruption

Cut cables leave shops unable to take card payments

Meg Houghton-Gilmour, food writer and founder of The Bristol Sauce, undertook a two-part research piece into the world of food influencing when she created a website and social media account for a fake Japanese restaurant "coming soon to Bristol".

She messaged 48 influencers asking how much they would charge to make content, what would guarantee positive coverage and whether they would declare it an advert.

After receiving 33 responses, she said the prices quoted by influencers varied widely. Some said they would post in exchange for free food and drink, without an extra payment on top - and five of those said they would post without labelling the content as an advert.

UK advertising rules state paid posts must be clearly marked with #ad or a platform's paid partnership feature. This includes free meals in exchange for posts.

Houghton-Gilmour added the requests she sent out had created a swell of "misleading" positive noise on social media around the upcoming opening.

"I realised how insular and repetitive it is. Everyone going to the same places, saying the same thing," she said.

With more than 135,000 followers on Instagram and millions of views on TikTok , Oscar Bostock, also known as Bos Finesse, is a driving force as a food creator in Bristol and said becoming an influencer was a "no-brainer".

"There are food creators in the social media space, like myself, who do have a lot of credibility. But we need to respect the culture a bit as well.

"You'll never beat the people that write about food for a living. I don't really like to review and criticise food - I'll leave that to the professionals.

"At the same time, you need people here like myself to just celebrate food," he adds.

Bostock says authenticity is very important to him, and told the BBC there are many places he has said no to reviewing or reflecting.

"It's worth explaining it, being paid for a restaurant to say, 'this is good' is completely different to being paid to promote a new menu or venue.

"I feel very strongly about it, anywhere I work with had to be a place I actually valued and would visit in my own time."

Food critic Jay Rayner, who writes for the Financial Times, believes his role is to write "as interesting, entertaining [and] truthful column" as he can.

"I don't think there's much truth in the idea that the newspaper critic is dead," he said. "What I see happening is an awful lot more media around restaurants, full stop.

"I know, anecdotally, that a good review from me still results in many bookings, which is lovely - but it's not actually a concern of mine."

He said people sometimes ask if influencers "pose a challenge to what you do".

"My response is, 'only if it's better than what I do'," said Rayner, stressing his authority as a critic is not unassailable. "I do not have a right to my lofty perch."

Rayner said newspapers such as the Financial Times would "pick up the bill" for critics writing reviews, whereas a lot of influencers were invited to eat for nothing, which is something consumers should be aware of.

"That does undermine the credibility of the review," he said. "[But] you know, we're all celebrating the culture of eating food and eating out."

Adam Armstrong, head chef at Bath's Emberwood, said the sort of promotion restaurants received from influencers was something the industry would have been "screaming out for" years ago.

"If you make a bit of noise here or there, it just puts you on the map," he said.

He acknowledged many people had a "negative" view of food creators, but added: "People give them too much reverence in the first place. They're just people with an opinion."

The Nook Cheltenham, in Gloucestershire, has worked hard at being Instagram-friendly, currently boasting more than 11,000 followers.

Director and founder Edward Surman said: "Social media is a place where brands can alter their own story - where it's not moved around by the press."

Surman maintains influencers are not replacing food critics, but more of an "augmentation".

Wiltshire-based food influencer Baljinder Kaur Sangha-Gill, also known as The Authentic Punjabee, says her pages have moved beyond a list of recommendations and have come to represent a community of friends.

"Influencers haven't replaced critics. We've just opened the conversation about food," she said.

"Years ago, when you were looking for a restaurant or recipe, you'd wait for the Sunday paper. Now you can just go onto TikTok."

But she cautions not everything on social media is reliable.

"People will get free things to promote something. You've got to be aware of that. I'm very careful with that, I don't lie to my followers," she added.

Following her research, Houghton-Gilmour added: "Influencers are a symptom of the society and tech world we live in - not the problem. It's the tech billionaires making it unclear what's an ad and what's not."

She said the problem was not people making content but the lack of transparency, although she accepted that was not true of all influencers.

articles.title: "El Cacas" Kenia Os se confiesa con Rosalía en concierto de CDMX
articles.standfirst: La cantante mexicana fue invitada de lujo a la presentación de la española
articles.summary: La cantante mexicana fue invitada de lujo a la presentación de la española
articles.body: La experiencia de los conciertos de la cantante española, Rosalía, no se remiten únicamente a vivir e interpretar con mucha pasión sus grandes éxitos, la realidad es que este es un espectáculo integral y una de las dinámicas que no solamente el público que asiste disfruta, sino que además de vuelve viral pronto en redes sociales es la del llamado ‘Confesionario’, en donde la también compositora invita a otra celebridad que saca a la luz un tema escabroso de su vida personal y en su primera presentación en la Ciudad de México, el turno fue para una colega suya, Kenia Os. La nacida en Mazatlán, Sinaloa, el 15 de julio de 1999 (27 años de edad), cuyo nombre real es Kenia Guadalupe Flores Osuna, ha literalmente encendido las redes sociales y es que ha hecho público una infidelidad de la que fue víctima hace algún tiempo, no sabemos cuándo y no sabemos exactamente a quién se refiere, pero si tenemos una gran e interesante especulación, pero primera, repasemos que fue lo que dijo y que tiene a todo el mundo atentos al chisme. “Ninguna de mis relaciones ha funcionado porque soy una mujer que pongo límites, digo lo que no me gusta y, bueno, todo este tipo de cosas que me hacen ser una mala mujer, obviamente, sabes”, dijo Kenia Os en el Palacio de los Deportes el pasado sábado por la noche. “Hoy vamos a hablar de un cacas”. “Yo estaba en un tour, yo iba a dejar el país por bastantes semanas, era un tour muy importante, mi tour por primera vez en Estados Unidos. Entonces, como buenas personas, cantantes que se están conociendo, nos prometimos paz, tranquilidad, armonía, nada de cosas turbias, lo típico”, aseveró durante el evento que corresponde al LUX Tour 2026. “De repente me doy cuenta que él etiqueta a una mujer, en oculto. ¿Cómo me di cuenta? Tengo muchas amigas y muchos gays. Obviamente le pregunté por qué etiquetarla en oculto, no me hablaste nada de ella. No me quiero ver loca, pero necesito un poquito mi espacio porque nos estamos conociendo, como buen hombre me dijo: ‘Nada que ver’, ‘estás loca, ni al caso’, ‘jamás andaría con ella’. Acto seguido, en ese tiempo que nos estábamos dando, tiempo muy corto, o sea, como 10 días, comienza a salir con ella”.

articles.title: Ester Expósito desvela por qué ya no hace escenas íntimas: "Hice suficientes en 'Élite"
articles.standfirst: La actriz explica que hay muchos proyectos en las que “hay escenas de sexo gratuitas”
articles.summary: Ester Expósito desvela por qué ya no hace escenas íntimas: "Hice suficientes en 'Élite"
articles.body: Ester Exposíto lleva años labrando una gran carrera como actriz. Una trayectoria que comenzó mucho antes de sus papeles en ‘Élite’. Su primera aparición en pantalla fue en la serie ‘Centro médico’. En la actualidad, ya es una de las actrices más reconocidas del panorama español. Tal y cómo explica en una conversación con Hugo Diego García organizada por GQ España, ese reconocimiento ha llevado a Ester a poder elegir o rechazar algunos proyectos por muchas razones, entre ellas, que considere que en el guion aparezcan ”muchas escenas de sexo gratuitas”. “Ya hice suficientes en ‘Élite’”, declara Expósito, “entiendo que era parte del producto, de cómo era, pero es verdad que luego decidí protegerme un poco más”. En la ficción juvenil de Netflix, los actores interpretaban a compañeros de instituto y se mostraban los comportamientos que se suelen tener en el ámbito privado a esa edad. “No hay nada de malo, porque al final en el cine o en la televisión retratamos la vida, y en la vida hay sexo, como también hay violencia”, explica la intérprete sobre la aparición de escenas íntimas en el cine. “No es que me niegue a tener escenas íntimas, pero sí que me niego a tenerlas cuando no son necesarias para contar la historia y son gratuitas o demasiadas”, concluye la actriz. Después Hugo le pregunta sobre cómo vive ella sus relaciones personales. “He tenido un proceso y un camino, porque yo creo un poco por la cosa que tenemos instaurada todavía del amor romántico y de que el amor duele”, comienza contestando Ester. “Mis relaciones siempre fueron un poco turbulentas. He tenido momentos felices, pero mis relaciones en el pasado siempre han sido muy intensas, muy dramáticas…”. Ahora, confiesa que ha madurado y que está en un momento muy feliz.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Woody Allen: âThe talent for being happy is appreciating and liking what you have, instead of what you donât have,' the âAnnie Hallâ starâs words on finding happiness in what you already have
articles.summary: Explore Woody Allen's profound quote on happiness and learn how appreciating what you already have can lead to a more fulfilling life. Discover his journey and career achievements in the entertainment industry.
articles.body: Woody Allen has been a well-known figure in the entertainment industry for years. The star dabbled in everything, ranging from acting to directing and writing. Todayâs quote about learning how to be satisfied with life and what you already have comes from a place of experience for Allen.The quote of the day by Woody Allen reads, "The talent for being happy is appreciating and liking what you have, instead of what you donât have.âWhat did Woody Allen mean by this quote?This quote is directly from the filmmaker and actorâs book titled âWoody Allen on Woody Allen: In Conversation with Stig BjÃ¶rkman.â The quote essentially says that it is important to appreciate what you already have, rather than focusing on what you do not. While it is human nature to appreciate things you have not yet achieved more, it often results in people forgetting the things they once worked hard to achieve.He acknowledges that one should never stop striving for success and goals; however, the key to success is remembering where you came fromâyour roots. When happiness is attached to what you don't have, the finish line keeps moving. Obtaining the missing piece simply creates a new desire, leaving you forever dissatisfied with life.At the end of the day, focusing on existing relationships, current health, or present comforts and things you have anchors you in the moment. It transforms routine aspects of life into sources of genuine joy and helps you understand that you need a balance of wanting more, while also appreciating what you already have.About Woody Allenâs early lifeHeywood âWoodyâ Allen (born Allan Stewart Konigsberg) was born in Brooklyn, New York, on December 1, 1935. His mother worked as a bookkeeper, while his father was a waiter and also engraved jewelry. Woody had humble beginnings and was from a middle-class family. Over the years, the filmmaker and actor has been open about how his relationship with his parents was strained and that he did not connect well enough with them. As a child, he immersed himself in the arts to escape his turbulent childhood. This included reading comic books, listening to jazz radio, doing magic tricks, and playing the clarinet.From an early age, he was interested in filmmaking and studied the subject at NYU (from where he later dropped out after failing a class) and City College of New York. He also legally changed his name to Heywood Allen when he was 17 and started calling himself by the nickname, âWoody.âWoody Allenâs careerHe started in the industry writing for âThe Herb Shriner Show,' after which he also wrote for âThe Tonight Showâ and âCandid Camera.' He received his first Grammy nomination for his self-titled comedy album. He dabbled in Broadway, working on âDon't Drink the Waterâ and âPlay It Again, Sam.â He entered the film industry as a screenwriter with âWhat's New, Pussycat?â and the rest is history. Over the years, he has worked as a scriptwriter, filmmaker, director, and actor. His first time as a director came with âWhat's Up, Tiger Lily.'Over the course of his career in the entertainment industry, Allen has scored more than 75 writing credits, along with over 50 directing credits and 50 acting credits.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.body: Prince William was reportedly "blindsided" by Prince Harry and Meghan Markle’s surprise decision to return to the U.K. with their children. Several royal experts told Fox News Digital that the Prince and Princess of Wales are "concerned" about the Duke and Duchess of Sussex returning for an extended period beginning this month. Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet are set to begin school there in September, People magazine reported. "Prince William was blindsided," Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital. PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE’S UK MOVE PUTS FRESH SPOTLIGHT ON THEIR EXPLOSIVE CLAIMS AGAINST ROYAL FAMILY "He had found Harry’s recent eagerness to publicly signal that he wanted to spend more time in Britain unusual, but that is very different from anticipating a full return. William now has to navigate a situation he did not create, did not ask for and, given the state of their relationship, almost certainly would not have chosen." Fox News Digital reached out to Kensington Palace for comment. In a statement shared with The New York Times, a spokesperson for the Sussexes said, "On the heels of a wonderful trip with family and friends this summer, Harry and Meghan have decided to spend an extended period in the U.K. this autumn. They are excited to have their children spend more time in the country that’s such an important part of their family’s story." The spokesperson confirmed that the couple’s businesses will remain unchanged and based in the U.S. Meghan and Harry will also keep their home in California. "Prince William is said to feel that Harry and Meghan have spent years attacking the institution, then monetizing their grievances through a very lucrative media operation. From his view, it’s an ongoing campaign for maximum impact and self-gain. He’s not going to fuel it, and he’s not going to endorse behavior he sees as damaging." William and Kate were seen arriving in Scotland on Thursday, where they’ll spend time with King Charles at Balmoral Castle. The royal family has spent summers at the Scottish estate since the reign of Queen Victoria, with family members traditionally hunting, fishing and horseback riding there. The king learned about Harry and Meghan’s move three days before it was made public, according to reports. "Prince William, along with Catherine, is currently at Balmoral Castle visiting the king," royal broadcaster Neil Sean told Fox News Digital. "Harry and Meghan have, so far, not been invited to visit the king privately while on a holiday. This will not happen while William is there. I’ve been told he has no desire to connect on any level with his younger brother and simply has no time for [Meghan]." Fox News Digital reached out to Archewell, which handles the offices of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, for comment. Several royal experts previously told Fox News Digital that William and Harry haven’t been on speaking terms since at least 2022. articles.body: Amid the ongoing row over Maharashtra's new rule making Marathi mandatory for commercial vehicle drivers, actress Sonam Kapoor has reacted to the controversy on social media. Her response comes as transport officials continue assessing drivers across Mumbai and the surrounding region, with hundreds found unable to speak the language. Let's learn more about it.Sonam Kapoor's reactionReacting to the development, Sonam Kapoor commented on a post by a journalist, simply writing, "Huh."What the transport assessment foundSince August 20, transport officials have assessed 5,211 drivers, including 3,942 across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. Among those checked in the MMR, 722 drivers were found unable to speak Marathi and were subsequently issued notices. The Maharashtra State Transport Department had set August 15 as the deadline for drivers to learn Marathi after making knowledge of the language mandatory.Drivers go on strikeMumbai autorickshaw drivers began a three-day strike on Monday to oppose the government's rule, saying it could increase their financial burden, especially for those with limited formal education. Protesters also blocked traffic on Kandivali Link Road, raising concerns over the language requirement and penalties for non-compliance. Several drivers said older members of the community were finding it difficult to learn Marathi within the given deadline.What's next for Sonam Kapoor?Away from the controversy, Sonam Kapoor is yet to return to the big screen. She married Anand Ahuja in 2018 and welcomed their first son, Vayu, in August 2022, followed by their second son, Rudralokh, on March 29. The actress' last film was 'Blind' in 2023, and she was earlier expected to star in the screen adaptation of 'Battle For Bittora'.'Blind' was backed by Sujoy Ghosh and also featured Purab Kohli, Vinay Pathak and Lillete Dubey in supporting roles. articles.body: A major tribute is set to come up in Theni district for one of Tamil cinemaâs most respected filmmakers, Bharathiraja. The Tamil Nadu Government has announced plans to build a memorial hall in his birthplace, complete with a bronze statue. The announcement has now received appreciation from actor and Rajya Sabha MP Kamal Haasan, who praised the government for recognising the directorâs contribution to Tamil cinema. The proposed memorial is being seen as a fitting tribute to a filmmaker who brought the lives, emotions and landscapes of rural Tamil Nadu to the screen.Kamal Haasan hails TN governmentâs Bharathiraja memorial planKamal Haasan took to X to welcome the Tamil Nadu Governmentâs decision. He expressed his gratitude for honouring Bharathiraja in the land where the filmmaker was born. âMy heartfelt congratulations to the Tamil Nadu government for announcing that a memorial hall will be established in the very soil of his birth for director Bharathiraja, who captured the scent of the earth on screen. This is a gratitude rendered in the fullness of time,â Kamal Haasan said in his post. articles.title: Kate Hudson to produce How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days sequel, 23 years on
articles.summary: Hudson and Matthew McConaughey, her co-star from the 2003 rom-com, could be reunited for the sequel.
articles.body:
A sequel to How to Lose a Guy In 10 Days is in development, more than 20 years after the original hit rom-com was released, with original star Kate Hudson set to produce.

Work on the film is in the "very early days", with sources telling US media , external that both Hudson, 47, and Matthew McConaughey, 56, could reprise their roles from the first film.

In the original, Hudson played a magazine journalist called Andie who researches an article about modern dating. She convinces her boss she can get a man, Benjamin (McConaughey), to leave her in 10 days. Meanwhile, Benjamin bets his boss he can make any woman fall for him, with Andie his target.

Hudson will produce the sequel alongside Stacey Sher, who is behind hits such as Pulp Fiction and Matilda.

The movie grossed nearly $180m worldwide at the box office at the time.

The yellow silk Carolina Herrera dress Hudson wore near the end of the film also became a much talked-about piece of modern cinema fashion.

The star's most recent film role was in 2025's Song Sung Blue, which earned her a second Oscar nomination, following her first nod for Almost Famous back in 2001.

McConaughey's films include Dallas Buyer's Club, which won him an Oscar in 2014, The Wedding Planner and Magic Mike. He also appeared in 2008 movie Fool's Gold alongside Hudson.

Representatives for Hudson and McConaughey have been contacted for comment.

The new film would be the latest in a trend for nostalgic sequels in Hollywood, following The Devil Wears Prada 2 - which came 20 years after the original and also featured a magazine employee called Andy (played by Anne Hathaway).

In 2024, McConaughey told People magazine about his first meeting with Hudson before filming How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days.

"Immediately, we were comfortable with each other, and we jacked with each other, and we busted each other's chops, and we laughed a lot," he recalled.

"There was a bit of rock and roll exchange, like, 'Oh, this could be some heavyweight fun.' And I think that's why I was cast, and that's why, for whatever extent, it worked."

articles.title: 'How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days' is coming back. Here's where 7 other 2000s rom-com revivals stand.
articles.summary: Paramount is developing a follow-up to the beloved rom-com, with hopes that Kate Hudson and Matthew McConaughey will reprise their roles.
articles.body:
After a real chick flick drought in recent years, fans of the genre are being treated to a whole slate of 2000s romantic-comedy sequels. The latest? The iconic How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days . Paramount Pictures is in early development on a follow-up to the 2003 movie, a source close to the project has confirmed to Deadline .

Hudson is producing alongside Stacey Sher, while Paramount and the filmmakers hope that Hudson and Matthew McConaughey will reprise their roles. However, no cast members are attached, and the project is still seeking a screenwriter, according to reports.

In the original movie, magazine writer Andie Anderson (Hudson) dates advertising executive Ben Barry (McConaughey) for an article about how to drive a man away in 10 days, unaware that he has bet he can make her fall in love with him in the same period. As is the rom-com way, they're bound for love, and their competing schemes become complicated when real feelings develop.

The film was a big hit, grossing over $178 million globally against a reported $50 million budget. Critics were less enthusiastic, with the film currently holding a 42% rating on Rotten Tomatoes , but audiences responded far more favorably. McConaughey said on the Happy Sad Confused podcast that it's the film that provides him with the most residual income.

"I think it's probably my favorite rom-com I've done, and a lot of people love that rom-com," McConaughey told host Josh Horowitz earlier this month . "And it still pays the best mailbox money of any film I've ever done. By far. By lengths."

No release date has been announced for the How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days sequel — and it remains to be seen whether Andie and Ben invested in a second "love fern" and managed to keep it alive — but several other 2000s rom-com revivals are also being developed or discussed.

A third installment (after 2004's The Princess Diaries: Royal Engagement ) is in development, with Anne Hathaway returning as teen-turned-princess Mia Thermopolis. Whether Chris Pine, Héctor Elizondo and Heather Matarazzo reprise their roles remains to be seen, but we know for certain that Julie Andrews won't be back .

A follow-up to the soccer film that gave Keira Knightley her breakthrough role is also in development, with the original film's cowriter and director, Gurinder Chadha, working on a sequel . It's unknown whether Knightley or her colead, Parminder Nagra (who played Jesminder "Jess" Bhamra), will return — it all hinges on the strength of the script, Chadha told Deadline last year.

A tale of adolescence, adulthood and what's really important in life, this Jennifer Garner classic had viewers joining in the "Thriller" dance and wanting Mark Ruffalo as their boyfriend (that hasn't changed). Earlier this summer, Netflix announced a reimagining of the movie is coming , with People We Meet on Vacation 's Emily Bader and The Perks of Being a Wallflower's Logan Lerman leading a new cast. Garner is on board as an executive producer, and while she and original costar Judy Greer have also been photographed filming scenes for the project, the exact nature of their roles hasn't been confirmed.

A festive favorite, The Holiday 's star-studded ensemble included Cameron Diaz, Kate Winslet, Jude Law and Jack Black. Last year, it was announced that Apple TV+ has a limited series adaptation in the works, but none of the original cast or Nancy Meyers, who wrote and directed the original, are said to be involved. Instead, the revival will use the same plot: An American woman and a British woman swap homes and lives for the holidays, ultimately finding love.

This high school revenge comedy starred some of the biggest names of the moment: Jesse Metcalfe, Sophia Bush, Ashanti, Arielle Kebbel, Penn Badgley and Brittany Snow. A sequel was first talked about in 2024 , when Kebbel said "there is a script" that "does involve all the OG cast," but in February, Kebbel revealed during a podcast interview that the project, which she was developing and producing, is "on pause for now."

During a hiatus from Grey's Anatomy , Katherine Heigl filmed her lead role in 27 Dresses as Jane, who was a bridesmaid in 27 weddings while quietly longing for love herself. In May 2025, Heigl said she was "in talks" about a sequel but added that it would "have to be done right." Her love interest in the movie, James Marsden, confirmed he's open to reprising his role too. "That movie weirdly has legs that I'm not sure I anticipated it having," Marsden told E! News in 2023. "Just a fanbase that people — when they talk about romantic comedies — you don't really see too many of those made nowadays."

There are only so many times a singer can post himself dancing to the same song before people start scrolling past. Jamie Miller seems to have found a way to fix that: by bringing in celebrity dance partners.

The Welsh singer has been promoting his infectious new song, "Babydoll," on TikTok and Instagram by two-stepping to the track in video after video. Lately, though, the people dancing alongside him have gotten a lot more recognizable. Jennifer Love Hewitt was the first famous face to join him. Dancing With the Stars ' Julianne Hough then followed, as did Antonio Cipriano , one of the breakout stars of Prime Video's series Off Campus .

Love Hewitt, in particular, really got into "Babydoll," using it in several TikToks and posting a video of herself playing it on the piano. "Playing around with it makes me smile," she wrote in the Aug. 12 post, thanking Miller for the song. Just days later, she was dancing alongside him , with Miller dubbing her "the most iconic babydoll there is."

The upbeat track was released Aug. 7, although Miller had been teasing it by posting snippets since late July. Now, each new "Babydoll" video comes with a question: Who will Miller get to join him next? Viral dances can come and go quickly, but rotating cameos give the same song a reason to keep popping up on people's feeds: it's the ideal formula for keeping a viral moment going.

Singer Role Model pulled off something similar with his track "Sally, When the Wine Runs Out," bringing a different "Sally" onstage during performances. Celebrities including Natalie Portman, Olivia Rodrigo and Charli xcx all took a turn, and clips of the cameos routinely went viral. Finding out who Sally would be became part of the attraction.

Sabrina Carpenter put her spin on the celebrity reveal during her Short n' Sweet tour, jokingly "arresting" famous faces for "being too hot" before singing "Juno." Millie Bobby Brown, Gigi Hadid and Salma Hayek were among those who got cuffed.

For anyone just discovering Miller through "Babydoll," he's been around for a while. The 28-year-old appeared on The Voice U.K. in 2017, where he competed on Jennifer Hudson's team and finished third. He released his debut album, titled Long Way Home , in 2024, but it did not chart on the Billboard 200.

Earlier this year, he signed with Republic Records , which is home to many of pop's biggest names, including Taylor Swift, Ariana Grande and the Weeknd. He has a sizable social media fanbase, including 4.1 million followers on TikTok and 1.2 million on Instagram — but "Babydoll" has put a new level of attention on the singer.

Love Hewitt has been posting about "Babydoll" enough that people have started wondering if she's on the record company's payroll. "People have asked me, 'Why are you putting it in all of your videos, besides the fact that it's addicting? Why are you pushing this song so much? Do you work for his record company?'" she said in a TikTok posted Aug. 23.

Love Hewitt clarified that she didn't work for his record company and said she first heard "Babydoll" on a day that "was not great." "Music finds you when you really need it," she said, and the song changed her mood: "The day was instantly better, more manageable, full of light."

Then she got to know Miller. "He is light. He is magic," the actor said. The first time they met in person was when they filmed their video together. Love Hewitt is clearly rooting for him now. "He is such a pure, kind, good human, who has worked so hard for this moment," she said. "We are all collectively gathering around him, rooting for him, becoming his magical, positive light army in the world."

How long the "Babydoll" moment lasts is anyone's guess. But for now, Miller has something plenty of singers would envy: a growing audience waiting to see what happens next.

articles.body: Veteran filmmaker Kuku Kohli, best known for launching Ajay Devgnâs career with Phool Aur Kaante, has passed away at the age of 77. He suffered a cardiac arrest on Tuesday evening. His wife, actress Aruna Iraniâs spokesperson, has confirmed the news to ETimes.Since Aruna Irani was not in a state of mind to speak, her spokesperson shared details about what had happened.According to the spokesperson, Kuku Kohli felt restless on Monday night and suffered a mild heart attack. He was admitted to Kokilaben Hospital that same night, where he underwent an angioplasty. Everything appeared to be normal after the procedure. However, on Tuesday at around 5:15 pm, he suffered a massive cardiac arrest.Meanwhile, Aruna was on a call with him and exchanging messages, and the two were reportedly in a playful mood. He even told her, âLetâs not go overboard.â Shortly afterwards, however, he began showing signs that something was wrong. After some time, he stopped responding.The final rites of veteran filmmaker Kuku Kohli will take place on Wednesday, August 26, at Oshiwara Crematorium in Andheri West. His funeral procession will leave his residence at Green Acres, Lokhandwala Complex, Andheri West, at 10 am.Who was Kuku Kohli?Born Avtar Kohli on June 4, 1949, in Peshawar, Kuku Kohli was a director, writer, editor and screenwriter who spent more than three decades in the Indian film industry. Early in his career, he worked closely with legendary filmmaker Raj Kapoor, assisting him on films including Bobby, Prem Rog and Satyam Shivam Sundaram, where he honed his craft.He later served as second-unit director on Betaab, the film that launched Sunny Deol and Amrita Singh, and subsequently worked on Arjun, starring Sunny Deol and Dimple Kapadia.His biggest breakthrough came with Phool Aur Kaante in 1991, which marked Ajay Devgnâs debut as a leading actor and went on to achieve diamond jubilee status at the box office.A career spanning several hitsFollowing the success of Phool Aur Kaante, Kohli went on to direct several notable films, including Kohraam, starring Dharmendra, and Suhaag, featuring Ajay Devgn, Akshay Kumar and Karisma Kapoor.He also directed Haqeeqat, starring Ajay Devgn, Tabu and Amrish Puri. The film received seven nominations, including a Best Director nomination.His other works included Zulmi, starring Akshay Kumar and Twinkle Khanna, and Anari No. 1, which he co-produced with his wife.Kuku Kohliâs personal lifeKuku Kohli married veteran actress Aruna Irani in 1990. The couple reportedly did not have children together. This was Kohliâs second marriage, and he had two daughters from his first marriage to Rita Kohli.His passing marks the end of an influential chapter in Bollywoodâs commercial cinema of the 1990s, an era he helped shape through his collaborations with several leading stars of the time.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.standfirst: El experimentado cocinero enumera las claves para conseguir un óptimo resultado de este clásico del verano
articles.summary: El experimentado cocinero enumera las claves para conseguir un óptimo resultado de este clásico del verano
articles.body: El periodo estival empieza a llegar a su fin, pero aún queda tiempo para elaborar las últimas recetas de los clásicos de este tiempo. El rey, por encima de todos, es el salmorejo. Jordi Cruz, chef y jurado de ‘MasterChef’, ha compartido en sus redes sociales los pasos que hay que seguir para conseguir el salmorejo perfecto con una receta “sencilla” y con “pocos ingredientes”. Lo primero que deja claro es que su salmorejo no lleva pimiento y tampoco vinagre, aunque matiza que esto es “un toque personal”. Para empezar con un buen pie en la elaboración, debemos procurar que “todos los ingredientes estén muy fríos antes de empezar”. Incluso, recomienda que puedes dejar el tomate cortado unos 20 minutos en el congelador. Después, hay que preparar la base del plato: “Tritura el tomate, el pimiento rojo (si decides utilizarlo) y el ajo sin germen hasta obtener una mezcla completamente fina”. Aunque hay personas que prefieren no añadir pan, Cruz sí lo incluye en su receta. Además, puntualiza que sea del “día anterior”. También se debe añadir en este momento la sal. “Con la trituradora en marcha, añade el aceite de oliva virgen extra poco a poco, en forma de hilo, hasta obtener una crema muy fina y sedosa”, apunta. También es gusto personal pasarlo por un colador, para eliminar posibles pieles o semillas y conseguir una textura todavía más elegante, antes de servirlo en la mesa. Por último, Jordi Cruz comparte un pequeño detalle para que la receta sea aún más perfecta y equilibrada: “Si utilizas pimiento rojo, aprovecha únicamente la carne y evita las semillas y las partes blancas del interior. Aporta un ligero dulzor y un extra de sabor sin alterar la receta”.

This isn't a career that's like, 'Hey, you're 60, you're 55, you're 43, come on, let's pay you more than you've ever made.' You know what I mean? That's not been traditionally the role. articles.title: Javier Bardem: "España es donde quiero estar, donde vivo, donde cotizo, donde quiero que mis hijos crezcan"
articles.standfirst: El actor se sincera en una entrevista para promocionar 'El ser querido'
articles.summary: El actor se sincera en una entrevista para promocionar 'El ser querido'
articles.body: Javier Bardem ha reivindicado su amor por el cine de España y por el propio país. "El cine español es mi cine, es el cine donde yo he crecido. Luego he tenido la oportunidad de trabajar fuera y eso es un lujo, pero, lo dije el otro día, yo nunca he vivido fuera, he vivido siempre en España", ha explicado en una entrevista a EFE. El actor ha insistido en que no tiene ninguna intención de alejarse de su país natal: "Es aquí donde yo quiero estar, donde quiero que mis hijos crezcan, donde vivo, donde cotizo, donde me preocupa más lo que pasa a todos los niveles. Es donde está mi familia, donde están mis hermanos, donde están mis amigos. Es todo". El actor, ganador de un Oscar al mejor actor de reparto por 'No Country for Old Men', en 2007, vive un gran momento profesional a sus 57 años. Javier Bardem es el protagonista de 'El ser querido', película dirigida por Rodrigo Sorogoyen que se estrena este miércoles en las salas de cine, después de presentarse en el festival de Cannes. El actor interpreta a Esteban Martínez, un director de cine, con un marcado carácter violento, y también un padre ausente. "Ese es el problema generacional que ha sufrido, que no fue educado para ser consciente del dolor que puede provocar", ha detallado Bardem en la entrevista. El artista ha definido la trama de 'El ser querido' como una historia de abandono. "Todos hemos sentido el abandono en algún momento de nuestra vida, incluso a veces por nosotros mismos. Para sentirse involucrado con la historia no hace falta haber sido abandonado por tu padre", ha argumentado Javier Bardem. La película de Rodrigo Sorogoyen se podrá ver también en los cines de Estados Unidos y Canadá, motivo de gran satisfacción para el director, como ha expresado en un comunicado.

articles.title: Muere Dolly Parton, legendaria cantante de country, a los 80 años
articles.standfirst: La causa de su fallecimiento no ha sido revelada, por el momento
articles.summary: La causa de su fallecimiento no ha sido revelada, por el momento
articles.body: Luto en el mundo de la música después de conocerse el fallecimiento de Dolly Parton a los 80 años. La causa de la muerte no ha sido revelada, pero su familia ya la ha despedido en su perfil oficial de Instagram a través de un vídeo en el que explica lo sucedido su sobrino, Bryan Seaver, en nombre de toda la familia. Brilló en la música country con más de 25 canciones que fueron número 1 en los Estados Unidos, muchas de ellas también en el mundo. "Falleció en paz hoy en Nashville", reza la descripción del post publicado. Su canción más conocida es ‘I Will Always Love You’, una balada que compuso tras romper su relación con Wagoner en 1974. Además, en 1992 interpretó junto a Whitney Houston la banda sonora de la famosa película ‘El guardaespaldas’. Otra canción por la que es muy reconocida es ‘Jolene’, de 1973, de la que un cantante como Miley Cyrus ha hecho covers. En el vídeo, su sobrino, Seaver, explica: “Una vida brillante como un diamante que resplandeció para que el mundo la viera, Dolly siempre será una inspiración no solo por su música atemporal y su prolífica obra como compositora, sino también por su ingenio, calidez y bondad que nos hicieron sentir a todos como en familia”. Continúa diciendo: “El legado de Dolly Parton es de amor, compasión y resiliencia. Con una carrera de siete décadas, inspiró a varias generaciones de artistas y fans con su música y un compromiso inquebrantable para hacer del mundo un lugar mejor. Sus canciones seguirán resonando en personas de todas las edades, y su labor filantrópica tendrá un impacto duradero”. La propia artista habló abiertamente de sus problemas de salud, lo hizo a través de un post en redes sociales. Todo comenzó el 28 de septiembre de 2025, cancelando seis conciertos en diciembre en el Caesars Palace de Las Vegas, en lo que era su regreso a los escenarios. Además, el 30 de septiembre no pudo asistir a la ceremonia de entrega de los Premios de los Gobernadores de la Academia de Artes y Ciencias Cinematográficas, donde iba a recibir el Premio Humanitario Jean Hersholt. “Como muchos de ustedes saben, he estado lidiando con algunos problemas de salud y mis médicos me dicen que debo someterme a algunos procedimientos. Como bromeé con ellos, debe ser hora de mi revisión de los 100.000 kilómetros, ¡aunque no es el típico viaje a mi cirujano plástico!”, dijo en su momento, bromeando. “Si bien podré seguir trabajando en todos mis proyectos desde aquí en Nashville, solo necesito un poco de tiempo para prepararme para el espectáculo, como dicen. Y no se preocupen por que deje el negocio porque Dios aún no ha dicho nada sobre parar. Pero creo que Él me está diciendo que baje el ritmo ahora para poder estar lista para más grandes aventuras con todos ustedes. Los quiero y gracias por su comprensión”. Sin embargo, el 5 de mayo de 2026, publicó otro post en el que mencionaba directamente qué es lo que le pasaba: “Estoy aquí para darles una actualización sobre mi salud, y tengo buenas noticias y un poquito de malas. Estoy respondiendo muy bien a la medicación y a los tratamientos y sigo mejorando cada día”. “Ya saben que les he contado antes que siempre he tenido problemas con los cálculos renales. Mi sistema inmunológico y digestivo se desajustaron completamente en los últimos dos años y que están trabajando para reconstruirlos y fortalecerlos y volver a estar en forma pront”, sentenció hace tres meses.

articles.title: Dolly Parton de qué murió: La leyenda del country falleció a los 80 años
articles.summary: Fallece la legendaria cantante.
articles.body: La legendaria cantante y compositora de música country Dolly Parton se despidió de los años 80, según anunció su familia. Su muerte fue anunciada por su sobrino Brian Seaver en Instagram. "Me imaginaba la tristeza de este momento, pero no la había sentido de verdad hasta ahora", dijo. "Es un homenaje, un homenaje que combina un orgullo absoluto con una profunda tristeza". Dolly Parton nació el 19 de enero de 1946 en Pittman Center, Tennessee, y creció en una familia numerosa en una cabaña de una sola habitación. Era una de doce hermanos, y su crianza en la zona rural de Tennessee se convirtió en una importante fuente de inspiración para sus composiciones. Su talento musical se manifestó a una edad muy temprana. De niña, actuaba en la televisión local y se presentó en el Grand Ole Opry de Nashville con tan solo 13 años. Tras graduarse de la escuela secundaria en 1964, Parton se mudó a Nashville y comenzó a forjar su carrera como compositora e intérprete. Su colaboración con Porter Wagoner la consolidó como una gran estrella de la música country, pero Parton finalmente se independizó para seguir su propio camino. Esta transición dio lugar a algunas de las canciones que definirían su legado, como Jolene y I Will Always Love You. La influencia de Parton superó con creces los límites tradicionales de la música country. Su éxito de 1980, "9 to 5", fue un gran éxito pop y, además, dio título a la película que protagonizó junto a Jane Fonda y Lily Tomlin. Posteriormente, apareció en películas como "Magnolias de acero" y "La mejor casa de putas de Texas". También fue una de las compositoras más exitosas comercialmente de la música estadounidense. Reuters informó que Parton vendió más de 100 millones de discos en todo el mundo, y 25 de sus canciones alcanzaron el número 1 en la lista de éxitos country de Billboard. Ganó 11 premios Grammy, incluyendo un premio a la trayectoria, y fue incluida en el Salón de la Fama del Rock & Roll en 2022. "I Will Always Love You" se convirtió en una canción particularmente significativa para su legado. Parton la escribió originalmente como una despedida a Wagoner, pero la exitosa versión de Whitney Houston la dio a conocer a otra generación y la convirtió en uno de los sencillos más exitosos comercialmente jamás grabados por una artista femenina. Los logros de Parton también se extendieron al mundo empresarial. Transformó un parque temático de Tennessee en Dollywood, que se convirtió en un importante destino turístico y una fuerza económica significativa en la región. Quizás su contribución más perdurable fuera del mundo del espectáculo fue la Biblioteca de la Imaginación de la Fundación Dollywood. Esta iniciativa de alfabetización, establecida en 1995, proporcionaba libros gratuitos a niños pequeños y, con el tiempo, se expandió más allá de Tennessee a varios países. El programa ha distribuido más de 150 millones de libros, según The Guardian. Parton también donó un millón de dólares para la investigación de la vacuna contra la COVID-19 en la Universidad de Vanderbilt en 2020, convirtiéndose en una importante patrocinadora financiera de la investigación vinculada al desarrollo de la vacuna de Moderna. Sus últimos años estuvieron marcados por nuevos proyectos. Su sitio web oficial destacó recientemente las certificaciones de su nueva música y una producción de Broadway, DOLLY: A True Original Musical, cuyo estreno estaba previsto para diciembre de 2026. Hasta el momento, la familia no ha confirmado la causa de la muerte de Dolly Parton. Sin embargo, la cantante había enfrentado severon problemas de salud en los últimos meses. Parton anunció repentinamente en mayo de 2026 que cancelaba un espectáculo en Las Vegas y añadio había estado recibiendo tratamiento para cálculos renales durante varios años. La muerte de Parton cierra uno de los capítulos más notables del entretenimiento estadounidense moderno. Logró desenvolverse con éxito entre la música country, el pop, el cine, la televisión, los negocios y la filantropía, manteniendo siempre una conexión con sus raíces de Tennessee, que la moldearon. Para generaciones de fans, su voz inconfundible, sus composiciones y su generosidad serán inseparables de la historia de la música estadounidense.

articles.title: There was only one Dolly Parton. See her remarkable life in photos.
articles.summary: Parton was the purest kind of pop icon, with an image and a sound that was universally beloved yet entirely her own.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton died in Nashville on Tuesday at the age of 80 , but her outsize legacy will live on. Over a peerless six-decade career as a country singer, songwriter, entertainer and entrepreneur, Parton transmuted her hardscrabble roots as the daughter of an illiterate Tennessee sharecropper into the purest kind of pop iconography: an image and a sound that was universally beloved yet entirely her own.

In 2019, the New York Times ran a story with the headline "Is There Anything We Can All Agree On?" The answer? "Yes: Dolly Parton."

Among the things that everyone agreed on was Parton's prodigious talent. A child performer on local radio and television programs, she first broke through, in 1966, with a single called "Dumb Blonde." "Just because I'm blonde, don't think I'm dumb," Parton sang in the chorus. "'Cause this dumb blonde ain't nobody's fool."

The song was written by someone else, but the sentiment would come to define Parton's layered public persona: a voluptuous, rhinestone-studded, bouffant-bewigged " Backwoods Barbie " who happened to be the shrewdest of businesswomen, the sharpest of lyricists and the most generous of philanthropists.

"I've created this and played it up — the makeup, the whole persona," Parton said in a 2002 interview . "But this isn't all I am. It's not even most of what I am. Hopefully people can see beneath the hair to know there's a brain, beneath the boobs to know there's a heart and behind all the other stuff to know there's some talent."

Parton penned most of her subsequent hits herself. She found early success duetting with fellow country singer Porter Wagoner, but struck out on her own in the mid-1970s after a string of solo singles — " Joshua ," " Coat of Many Colors ," " Touch Your Woman ," My Tennessee Mountain Home ," "Travelin' Man," "Jolene" — made the country Top 20.

In 1974, Parton wrote "I Will Always Love You" about her professional split from Wagoner; the song was a hit for Parton multiple times (1974, 1982, 1995), and eventually topped the charts for 14 weeks when Whitney Houston covered it for The Bodyguard soundtrack in 1992.

All told, Parton was the top-ranking female singer on country radio from 1967 to 1993, with a total of 25 No. 1 country singles. She published 3,000 songs in her lifetime, blazing a trail for other women along the way. "I can't imagine anybody, especially in country, who doesn't try to emulate Dolly in some way," singer-songwriter Emmylou Harris said in 2006.

The fact that Parton accomplished so much in music while also challenging cultural stereotypes, starring in movies, opening a theme park, funding education programs and emphasizing hope, resilience, empathy and acceptance, both on stage and off — it all made her easy to agree on. It's hard to imagine that anyone else could have pulled it off, or will ever come close again.

articles.title: STEVE DOOCY: The Dolly Parton I saw when the cameras stopped rolling
articles.summary: Steve Doocy reflects on interviewing Dolly Parton half a dozen times, revealing the professionalism and kindness she showed when cameras weren't rolling.
articles.body: On August 23, 2016, ten years ago this week, I was with Dolly Parton in New York City, and we were about to do a live segment on FOX & Friends. Just before we went on, I asked Dolly if I could take a selfie with her. She looked at me and said, "Why would you want a picture with little ol’ me?" DOLLY PARTON DEAD AT 80 AS COUNTRY MUSIC WORLD MOURNS BELOVED ICON WHOSE SONGS SHAPED GENERATIONS I laughed and said, "Hello…Dolly—you’re Dolly Parton!" That was Dolly. Over my years on "FOX & Friends," I was lucky enough to interview her probably half a dozen times. And here’s something people watching at home wouldn’t necessarily know: Dolly was always on time. Always prepared. Always a professional. In morning television, where guests sometimes arrive moments before they’re supposed to be on live TV—or occasionally after—that matters! Dolly showed up ready to go. And the minute the camera came on, so did that Dolly magic. She was funny, quick, kind and incredibly smart. She knew exactly what she wanted to say, but somehow never let an interview feel rehearsed. You could ask her a serious question and get a thoughtful answer, then a few seconds later she’d say something hilarious that nobody saw coming. DOLLY PARTON'S CALIFORNIA RETREAT WITH WIG ROOM AND DOLLYWOOD BIRDHOUSE LISTS FOR $1.95M She was simply great television. But what I remember most is that she was just as nice when the cameras weren’t rolling. For all her fame, Dolly always seemed to understand something important: being nice to people doesn’t cost a thing. Underneath the rhinestones, the big hair and that unmistakable Tennessee voice was a very savvy businesswoman. Dolly didn’t just build a career. She built an empire. She understood her audience, understood her brand and, most importantly, understood people. And somehow, through all that enormous success, she remained remarkably down-to-earth. A few years ago, I interviewed Dolly and my friend James Patterson about the novel they wrote together, "Run, Rose, Run". Later, when I toured James’ Florida home, he showed me one of his prized possessions: a guitar Dolly had given him, inscribed with a birthday message that ended, naturally, "I will always love you." That was Dolly, too. And there’s another connection I had completely forgotten until today. During the ALS Ice Bucket Challenge craze in 2014, Kenny Rogers was challenged by Lionel Richie. Kenny then nominated three people to go next: Garth Brooks, Dolly Parton…and me. To this day, I’m still not entirely sure how Steve Doocy wound up on a list with Garth Brooks and Dolly Parton—but I’m glad I did! Dolly was one of those rare people who seemed to be exactly the same person when the cameras were off as when they were on. Funny. Kind. Smart. Professional. And completely original. She wrote songs that generations know by heart. She became a legendary entertainer, songwriter and businesswoman. She gave away millions of books to children. And she never seemed to forget where she came from—or lose her wonderful ability to laugh at herself. For all her fame, Dolly always seemed to understand something important: being nice to people doesn’t cost a thing. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION I’m grateful our paths crossed so many times. And today, ten years later, I’m especially grateful I asked for that selfie. Godspeed, Dolly. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Thanks for the music, the laughs, the memories—and the kindness. There will never be another one quite like you. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM STEVE DOOCY

articles.title: From '9 to 5' to 'Steel Magnolias,' 5 Dolly Parton movies to revisit
articles.summary: Dolly Parton's legacy extended well beyond country music, with memorable film roles, original songs and performances that made her a Hollywood favorite.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton has died at age 80, her nephew and head of security, Bryan Seaver, announced in an Instagram video on Tuesday. While most people associate the Queen of Country with hits like "Jolene," "Coat of Many Colors" and "Islands in the Stream" — and will no doubt be streaming her music in the wake of her death — the icon's legacy extends into the world of film as well.

The blond, bubbly, rhinestone-loving Tennessee native appeared in numerous movies and provided music for many of them. The 1980 film 9 to 5 , which marked her acting debut, included her hit song of the same name and earned her an Oscar nomination for Best Original Song. But it was just the beginning of a memorable, albeit modest — she has about a dozen feature film credits, in addition to a slew of made-for-TV movies — acting career.

Eager to revisit Parton's filmography? Here's a refresher on her onscreen performances.

The 1980 comedy, directed by Colin Higgins, stars Parton alongside Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin as office workers who rebel against their sexist boss.

Parton wrote the song "9 to 5" while working on the film's set, after realizing that her long acrylic nails could mimic the sound of a typewriter . The track became one of the biggest hits of the decade and earned Parton her first Oscar nomination. (She would later be nominated again for Best Original Song for "Travelin' Thru," the theme song to the 2005 film Transamerica .)

The movie 9 to 5 later inspired a 1982 TV series that ran for five seasons, as well as a Broadway musical for which Parton wrote the music and lyrics. The film's feminist themes also created an enduring legacy, with a 2022 documentary, Still Working 9 to 5, exploring its impact on gender equity.

In a 2019 interview with the Los Angeles Times , Parton reflected on the film's message: "Just keep pushing, hoping for equal pay for equal work, getting the respect that we need. I'll always be about that."

How to watch: 9 to 5 is currently streaming on Philo and is available to rent or buy on Prime Video .

The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas (1982)

Parton's second film was also a commercial success, reteaming her with 9 to 5 director Colin Higgins. In the film, Parton portrayed Miss Mona, who must fight to save her "Chicken Ranch" brothel after a public campaign to shut it down. The film earned Parton a Golden Globe nomination for Best Actress. She also rerecorded her 1974 song "I Will Always Love You" for the film, which then dominated the country charts.

Parton was particularly excited to do the film due to her costar, Burt Reynolds. "They have to rewrite it a little for Burt and me, 'cause I said I wouldn't do it unless I got to kiss him," she joked in a 1980 interview with Roger Ebert , prior to filming.

But the shoot didn't meet her expectations. In her 1994 autobiography, she called the film's production "a miserable, spirit-numbing ordeal."

How to watch: The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas is currently available to rent or buy on Prime Video .

Can you imagine Sylvester Stallone as a country singer? In the musical comedy Rhinestone , which was co-written by Stallone, Parton's nightclub singer bets that she can turn New York City cabbie Nick (Stallone) into a crooner in order to get out of her dead-end contract.

While Stallone called Rhinestone "the most fun I ever had on a movie," the film was a flop, with the actor admitting that "silly comedy" didn't quite work for him. Still, the soundtrack, much of which was penned and performed by Parton, was a success , with the song "Tennessee Homesick Blues" reaching the top of the country charts and "God Won't Get You" peaking at number 10. Parton also scored a Grammy nod for "Tennessee Homesick Blues" in the Best Country Vocal Performance, Female category.

How to watch: Rhinestone is currently unavailable ondigital streaming. You can purchase a DVD copy on Amazon .

This ensemble film, about the lives of a group of Louisiana women based on the 1987 play of the same name, was a massive hit. It starred Parton as Truvy Jones, owner of a small-town beauty shop, alongside Sally Field, Shirley MacLaine, Olympia Dukakis, Daryl Hannah and Julia Roberts. The film earned Roberts her first Academy Award nomination.

"I thought this was the perfect role for me because if I had not made it in the business, I would have been a beautician because I would have had to have got discount prices on makeup and hair color and bleach, and all of that," Parton told Vanity Fair in 2020. "So I felt like Truvy. I felt like I was fit right in that spot, and I really liked the role that I played. And that was a huge success. I loved working with all those women."

Unlike Parton's other work, this one was not centered on music. Though Parton wrote the song "Eagle When She Flies" for the movie, the filmmakers ultimately chose not to use a theme song for the film . Instead, the track — hailed by Rolling Stone as one of the best of Parton's career — became the title song off her 1991 album.

How to watch: Steel Magnolias is currently available to stream free with ads on Pluto TV .

In this romantic comedy, Parton stars as a small-town woman who stumbles into a job giving advice on the radio in Chicago, and falls for the investigative journalist (James Woods) who begins looking into her background.

Ten of Parton's songs were used for the film's soundtrack, including a rerecording of her 1976 song "Light of a Clear Blue Morning."

In a 1992 press conference, Parton revealed that the script had come her way seven years before the film got made. Per Parton, the role was eventually given to her Steel Magnolias costar Roberts, who eventually passed, allowing Parton to pick it up.

"We certainly `Dollyized' it," Parton said at the time. "It was a wonderful script, but a lot of [the dialogue] was ad-libbed. I can't hardly not ad-lib when I get something like this."

She also spoke about how proud she was to do the film, which she felt embodied so much of who she was.

"If I died tomorrow and never did another movie, it's a way for my family, my nieces, the younger kids in my family to see me and say, 'OK, that was Dolly the songwriter, that was Dolly the singer, that was Dolly the producer of the songs, that was Dolly the personality, Dolly the attitude, Dolly the values, the principles, the sense of humor,'" she explained. "It's just some of everything that I am, more than anything I've ever done."

How to watch: Straight Talk is available to rent or buy on Prime Video .

A rep for the singer later issued a statement to People revealing that she had “bravely [faced] a brief battle with cancer.”"Dolly opened doors for singers, songwriters, musicians and dreamers from every walk of life," Seaver said. "By her example, we believed anything was possible.""She has always been on your television, your record player, your CD, and on your phone playlist, becoming an extended part of your family, whether you liked it or not," he added. Parton's death comes after she announced in May that she was canceling her Las Vegas residency, which was set to begin in September after already being postponed nine months. She cited unspecified health issues but told the public in a video on Instagram that she was "responding really well to meds and treatments" and "improving every day."Follow below for updates, remembrances and more.
